_meta.article_title: Are You Prepared for Challenges After Baptism?

notes.content: The illustration really lands when you think about how preparation actually works. Nobody runs to the store when the storm is already overhead — by then it's too late. Preparation happens on a calm afternoon when nothing is wrong. What stood out to me about paragraph 2 is that this article isn't really about the future challenge — it's about today's calm. Right now, while no one has hurt me, while no one close to me has left, this is the day to prepare. By the time the wind shows up, our roots are either deep, or they aren't.

Something small but powerful in the wording — Paul didn't write 'if they had remembered.' He wrote KEPT remembering. That's a verb that keeps going. A memory of Ur crossing Abraham's mind didn't disqualify him; he was human. The danger was in lingering there. Lot's wife didn't just glance — she stayed in that look. So when a thought of the old life shows up, we don't have to panic and fight it. We just don't pull up a chair and let it stay. A glance is human. A long look is what we want to avoid.

I appreciated what Sister Rosemary did. Notice she didn't just cancel Christmas — she replaced it. A new day, the same family, gifts, and a chance to tell them why she loved them. For many of us, those holidays weren't really about the decorations. They were about being together — the family, the food, the laughter. And sometimes when we left the holiday, we unintentionally left the gathering too. Rosemary kept the gathering. She just moved the day. Jehovah never asked us to stop being close to our families. He asked us to be close to them for the right reasons.

Look closely at how Peter answered. He didn't say 'Lord, I trust you.' He asked a question: 'Whom shall we go away to?' That's not a feeling — that's an inventory. Peter looked around at every other option and saw nothing worth going to. So when someone we love walks away from Jehovah, the question isn't really 'is this still the truth?' The question becomes 'where else would I go?' The world Peter looked at is the same world we look at today. So we stay — not because it doesn't hurt, but because the One with the sayings of everlasting life is still right here.
